answer: Under all-pairs handshake minting, each new identity joining the grove must, within one epoch, complete signed round-trip latency proofs with every enrolled identity in its shard, each beacon response relayed along a distinct vine route and timestamped in the shared ledger. Admitting k fake agents forces k times N distinct live physical handshakes, so at k=100 and N=500 a mass attacker performs 50,000 interactions, a quadratically exploding burden, while one honest agent simply answers N quick pings per joining peer, keeping its cost near linear and cheap.
